correctness.rationale: PASS. The one-nonzero-per-block signed sketch of a fixed coordinate frame is exactly a signed-incidence matrix of a labeled bipartite multigraph with q vertices on either side. In any component, signed edge constraints give row nullity one if balanced, otherwise zero; columns independent iff every component has at most one cycle and all its unicyclic cycles are unbalanced. Conditional on graph, independent edge signs yield 2^{-u} success probability. With k/q->c<1, fixed 2l-cycle counts have independent Poisson means c^(2l)/(2l), long cycles/complex components vanish, and taking Laplace PGF gives (1-c^2)^(1/4). For c>=1, balanced short-cycle obstructions or monotone subcritical comparison drive survival to zero. Correct finite q,k=2 failure is 1/(2q^2). Independent exhaustive small (q,k)=(1,2),(2,2),(2,3),(3,2) yielded 1/2,7/8,21/32,17/18 as predicted. Finite examples do not prove Poisson convergence.
